changes: Recast the end of the Introduction around three linked questions rather than an implicit list of endpoints.
Q1 asks whether recent-rain activity expands the realized community along both spatial and taxonomic axes.
Q2 is the central structural test: whether the four-component incidence allocation departs from a magnitude-matched uniform-activation null.
Q3 asks whether expansion materially erodes local pairwise-Sorensen differentiation.
Discussion now answers Q1-Q3 in the same order and closes with the general distinction between community amplification and community recruitment.
general_principle: Environmental pulses can recruit previously inactive spatial and taxonomic participation beyond what uniform amplification predicts, while retaining local compositional differentiation.
unchanged: all endpoints, coefficients and uncertainty intervals
uniform-activation null specification, Monte Carlo decision and smoothing sensitivities
